youtube_title: LaPorte, Indiana: the LaPorte weather anomaly – more rain, storms and hail?
youtube:
A scientist once suggested that industry near Chicago was adding to the rain and storms over LaPorte, Indiana. In 1968 he published 'The La Porte Weather Anomaly—Fact or Fiction?' in the Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society. From 1951 to 1965, he reported, LaPorte got 31% more precipitation, 38% more thunderstorms and 246% more hail days than stations around it. LaPorte sits about 30 miles downwind of the industry around Chicago and Gary, and he suggested its pollution was feeding the storms. Other scientists questioned the local weather observer's records. Later the anomaly faded, and it was never fully settled how much of it was real. Comment your town, and it could be next! #LaPorte #LaPorteIndiana #Weather #WeatherHistory #History #LaPorteAfterDark #Shorts

All pictures are drawn. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: S. A. Changnon Jr., 'The La Porte Weather Anomaly—Fact or Fiction?', BAMS 49(1), 1968; Holzman and Thom, 'The La Porte precipitation anomaly', BAMS 51, 1970; Changnon, 'More on the La Porte Anomaly: A Review', BAMS 61(7), 1980; Huff and Changnon, Illinois State Water Survey (1972); Cassity, MIT thesis (1969); Norwine, Indiana Academy of Science; Niyogi and Schmid, AMS (2014). More local history: https://laporteweathernow.com/history
